## Introduction

This report acts as a demo which outlines the features available in the RAP
Skeleton Lite. This can be used for the creation of simple HTML documents such
as background quality reports or quickly converting documents originally
produced in Microsoft Word.

`r f_borderline()`

## CSS file for NISRA branding

The `style.css` file, which is found in the project’s code folder is used to
specify the visual presentation and styling of this output. It has been written
to comply with NISRA and departmental branding material guidance and it has also
been written with accessibility guidance in mind.

Changes to the visual presentation of the document can be made by editing the
`style.css` file. More information on how to write CSS code can be found
[on the W3 schools website](https://www.w3schools.com/css/default.asp).

`r f_borderline()`

## NISRA banner

The banner, which can be seen at the very top of this document, is called using
the function:

```
`f_banner(title = "RAP Skeleton Lite Demo")`
```

This can be configured in the `config.R` script by changing the
value of `nics_theme`:

```
nics_theme <- "dof"
```

`nics_theme` accepts any of the following values: "teo", "daera", "dfc", "de",
"dfe", "dof", "dfi", "doh", "doj", "bso", "adr". Setting nics_theme to your
department will automatically update the relevant colours, logos, alt texts and
departmental links contained in the banner (and throughout the rest of the
document).

The title and subtitle can be defined when calling the function:

```
f_banner(title = "Rap Skeleton Lite Demo", subtitle = "Optional Subtitle")
```

`r f_borderline()`

## Custom boxes

You can enhance the visual presentation of your reports by embedding custom HTML
and CSS directly into your document. One way to achieve this is by using div
boxes to highlight specific data or information, as shown in the example below.

```
<div class="container">
  <div class="box">
      <div>Population registered with a health service dentist</div>
      <div class="value">70%</div>
  </div>
  <div class="box">
      <div>Pupils enrolled in pre-school education, 2022</div>
      <div class="value">22,558</div>
  </div>
```
```
<!--html_preserve-->
<div class="container">
  <div class="box">
      <div>Population registered with a health service dentist</div>
      <div class="value">70%</div>
  </div>
  <div class="box">
      <div>Pupils enrolled in pre-school education, 2022</div>
      <div class="value">22,558</div>
  </div>
<!--/html_preserve-->
```

How it works:

*	HTML structure: The code uses standard HTML for creating a grid of boxes. Each
box contains a title and a value, which can be customized based on your content.

*	CSS for styling: CSS has been added to `style.css` and is used to control the
layout, colours, spacing, and overall appearance of the boxes.

`r f_borderline()`

## Images

The NISRA logo as well as logos for all departments are found in the project
folder: `(.../rap-skeleton-lite/images/)`.  You should save any images you use in
this folder.

Call an image in your rmd file (ensuring your file path uses forward slashes)
using:

```         
{r image, fig.alt="text description of image"}

knitr::include_graphics("../example/example.png")
```
For example:

```         
{r image, fig.alt="NISRA logo"}

knitr::include_graphics("../images/NISRA_logo_bilingual_colour.png")
```

```{r image,fig.alt="NISRA logo"}

knitr::include_graphics("../images/NISRA_logo_bilingual_colour.png")

```

Alt text is required for images. If the image is purely for decoration, use fig.alt="" so that a screenreader will ignore it. Otherwise, include a short description of the image using fig.alt = "description". 

Alternatively, for more control over the formatting of your image you can use
HTML. This approach is especially useful if you need to customize how images are
displayed (e.g. setting width, height and alignment). Learn more about adding
images using HTML
[on the W3 schools website.](https://www.w3schools.com/html/html_images.asp#:~:text=The%20HTML%20%3Cimg%3E%20tag%20is%20used)

`r f_borderline()`

## Tables

This section has a number of basic tables. The Good Practice Team recommend that
only small demonstration tables should be included in the publication itself.
Demonstration tables are small tables which highlight one or two messages
clearly and are supported by commentary.

When it comes to accessibility, a good rule of thumb is to use a simple
structure. Use a simple table matrix with a single row of column headers
describing what is in each column. Other considerations are as follows:

-   don’t merge cells
-   don’t have blank rows or columns
-   every column should have a heading
-   make sure all headings and labels are visible
-   use consistent rounding
-   left align text, or row labels, right align numbers
-   use thousand comma separator
-   avoid abbreviations or make sure they are explained fully
-   use caption for table titles
-   put any data labels in the headings such as % or millions or STG
-   don’t use symbols such as \* or superscripts to create notes or explanations, use [note x]

### Table 1

The following code outputs a table using the Kable package. More help with kable
can be found in the
[Rmarkdown cookbook](https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown-cookbook/kable.html).

```{r, echo=TRUE, class.source = 'fold-hide', message=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
data.frame(
  Option_A = c(
    "Single (never married or never legally registered a civil partnership) ",
    "Married or in a legally registered civil partnership",
    "Separated (but still legally married or still legally in a civil partnership)",
    "Divorced or formerly in a civil partnership which is now legally dissolved",
    "Widowed or surviving member of a legally registered civil partnership",
    "No code required (for under 16s)"
  ),
  Option_B = c(
    "1",
    "2",
    "3",
    "4",
    "5",
    "6"
  )
) %>%
  select("Option A" = Option_A, "Option B" = Option_B) %>%
  kbl(escape = FALSE, align = "lr") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = TRUE)
```

### Table 2 (pagination)

For longer tables, you may want to use pagination. The following table is
created using the DT package.
[More help with the DT package can be found here](https://rstudio.github.io/DT/).

```{r, echo=TRUE, class.source = 'fold-hide', warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
datatable(df_mye_year_gender_t,
  # DT creates row numbers by default. Suppress to ensure all cols have a header
  rownames = FALSE,
  # Rename column headers to make them descriptive
  colnames = c(
    "Mid Year Ending",
    "Females",
    "Males",
    "NI Population Total"
  ),
  caption = paste0("Number of males and females making up the total NI
                   population from ", earliest_year, -latest_year),
  # left align first column and add thousand separator to numbers
  options = list(columnDefs = list(list(className = "dt-left", targets = 0)))
) %>%
  formatRound(c("Females", "Males", "All persons"),
    digits = 0, interval = 3,
    mark = ","
  )
```

## Inline R (automation of values)

You can automate the presentation of stats by using 'Inline R'.

This is where you write a single line of R code to place a single variable
within your report:

Creation of an example variable:

```{r}
example_stat <- mean(c(10, 14, 26, 87))
```

```
example_stat <- mean(c(10, 14, 26, 87))
```

Printing the example variable: `r example_stat`

Where "example_stat" can be a variable you have already defined earlier in your
code.

`r f_borderline()`

## Hyperlinks

Use descriptive link text rather than displaying a url, i.e. [NISRA](www.nisra.gov.uk) rather than https://www.nisra.gov.uk/.  When writing link text:

* make sure to use wording that describes the destination of a link, don't use 'here' or 'read more' as link text 
* if a link is a download, make sure to include the file type and size in the link text
* links should open in the same window by default 
* if a link opens in a new window, include "(opens in a new window)" in the link text

Add a hyperlink using:

```         
[Text to display](URL path)
```

Example:

```         
[GSS harmonisation standards and guidance](https://analysisfunction.civilservice.gov.uk/government-statistical-service-and-statistician-group/gss-support/gss-harmonisation-support/harmonised-standards-and-guidance/)
```

`r f_borderline()`

## Table of contents

### Header tags (h3)

A key element is using header tags to structure your document. Screen readers
use these to scan and navigate documents so it's important that headings are
tagged correctly. The colour used in these headings is #1460aa rather than NISRA
blue to meet accessibility standards.

-   the title of the document is tagged as h1, don't use elsewhere
-   don't use heading styles to format text that isn't a heading (for example to
emphasise a point)
-   don't use bold, colour or text size to create visual headings without
tagging at the appropriate level
-   don't skip any heading levels, follow order h1, h2, h3, h4

More detailed guidance on writing for web is available in the Drupal user manual
published by Dissemination Branch. You can find the
[Drupal user manual](https://nicsonline.sharepoint.com/sites/TM-DOF-NISRATEAM/SitePages/DISSEMINATION%20NISRA-Website.aspx?ct=1727952358098&or=Teams-HL&ga=1&LOF=1)
and [other accessibility guidance](https://nicsonline.sharepoint.com/sites/TM-DOF-NISRATEAM/SitePages/DISSEMINATION%20Accessibility.aspx?ct=1727952463891&or=Teams-HL&ga=1&LOF=1)
on NISRA Teams Channel.

The table of contents is initialised and the parameters are set using the
following code:

```         
html_document:
  toc: true
  toc_float: true
  toc_depth: 4
```

* toc – can be true or false, determines whether table of contents is shown
* toc_float – can be true or false, determines whether table of contents appears
at top of page or at the side
* toc_depth – enter a number, determines the level of nesting headings which
appear in the table of contents

Headings and sub headings are then defined and registered in the table of
contents using hash keys:

```
## Heading

### Subheading
```

### Example subheading

`r f_borderline()`

## Lists

Unordered lists can be created using \*, + and - symbols:

```         
* Item 1
* Item 2
    + Item 2a
        - Item 2a.a
        - Item 2a.b
    + Item 2b
* Item 3
    + Item 3a
```

Output:

-   Item 1
-   Item 2
    -   Item 2a
        -   Item 2a.a
        -   Item 2a.b
    -   Item 2b
-   Item 3
    -   Item 3a

Ordered lists can be created using numbers followed by the contents with a space
in between. Similar to unordered lists, you can add extra layers as needed:

```         
1. Item 1
2. Item 2
3. Item 3
    + Item 3a
    + Item 3b
```

output:

1. Item 1
2. Item 2
3. Item 3
    + Item 3a
    + Item 3b

`r f_borderline()`

```{js}

// Function to add tabs to table of contents

function tabOrder() {
  
  // Make side menu tabbable

  let headings = document.getElementsByClassName('tocify-item list-group-item');
  let sections = document.getElementsByClassName('section');
  
  for (let i = 0; i < headings.length; i ++) {
    headings[i].innerHTML = "<a href='#" + sections[i].id + "'>" + headings[i].innerHTML +  "</a>";
  }

  
};

// Instruct web browser to run above function when loaded
window.onload = tabOrder;
```
